findings.title: Emoji resize job calls a `downsize` signature that no longer exists
findings.description: `optimized_image.rb` now defines `self.downsize` twice: `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at lines 145-147 and `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at lines 149-151. Ruby keeps only the last definition. `resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with five arguments, which now raises `ArgumentError` (given 5, expected 3..4). The job is enqueued from `app/models/emoji.rb:73`, so the failure is asynchronous. Uploaded emoji stop being capped at 100x100, and the only trace is a job error log. No spec references `resize_emoji` or `ResizeEmoji`, so the suite does not catch it. Fix: keep one `downsize` and have the job pass a dimensions string, e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "100x100", opts)`.

findings.title: Existing JS test encodes the removed setting-driven limit
findings.description: The test sets `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb = 5` (line 55) and expects a 10 KB image to be rejected with `max_size_kb: 5` (line 60). `utilities.js:182` now hardcodes 10 MB and no longer reads the setting, so the image is accepted. `not(validUpload([image]))` and the alert assertion both fail. The diff does not touch this test. Either update the test to the new contract or revert the client change.

findings.title: Dead first `downsize` definition
findings.description: The `(max_width, max_height)` overload at lines 145-147 can never run, because the definition at 149-151 replaces it. Remove it. Otherwise it reads as a supported overload that does not exist.

findings.title: Client limits are hardcoded and no longer follow the settings
findings.description: `validateUploadedFile` now enforces a fixed 10 MB, not `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`. Both settings are `client: true` (`config/site_settings.yml:513-518`). Attachments above the admin's limit (default 3072 KB) now pass the client check and are rejected only by `lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-88`. The user does see the server's message, so this is recoverable. The 413 branch at `utilities.js:246` also shows "10 MB" whatever the configuration says. The same `10 * 1024` / `10.megabytes` value is repeated in three places (`utilities.js:182`, `utilities.js:246`, `uploads_controller.rb:55`) with no shared constant, so the values can drift. Derive these from the settings, or centralize the constant and make the message match what the server enforces.

findings.title: Conversion failures are ignored and the upload proceeds unchanged
findings.description: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` on failure (`optimized_image.rb:160-169`), but the loop discards the return value. A file that `convert` cannot read gets five `convert` + `ImageOptim` runs, and this runs inline on the synchronous API path (lines 15-16). After five attempts the untouched oversized file goes to `Upload.create_for`. The user gets only a generic size error from the validator, and nothing logs the conversion failure. Stop the loop when `downsize` returns `false` and log it.

findings.title: Truncated API downloads can now be "repaired" into a valid-looking image
findings.description: The API URL download cap is now a fixed `10.megabytes`. `FileHelper.download` does not raise when the cap is reached. It stops writing and returns a truncated file (`lib/file_helper.rb:18-20`). Before this change the cap equaled the image limit, so a truncated file was still over the limit and the validator rejected it. Now a truncated image enters the new downsize loop. If ImageMagick accepts the partial input, the output is under the limit and passes validation, so a corrupt image is stored with no error. I did not run this, so the outcome depends on how `convert` handles truncated input. Fix: have `FileHelper.download` signal truncation (raise or return nil) so the request is rejected.

findings.title: Animated-thumbnail setting is reused for uploaded originals
findings.description: The loop passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. That setting is documented as generating animated thumbnails (`config/locales/server.en.yml:1118`). If an admin disables it, animated GIFs over the limit are reduced to their first frame (`optimized_image.rb:129`, `#{from}[0]`, used when the animated path is not selected at line 155). The stored original loses its animation, and no setting describes that. Use a dedicated setting, or pass the behavior explicitly. Separately, the animated path passes `80%` to `gifsicle --resize-fit` (`optimized_image.rb:120`). I could not confirm that gifsicle accepts a percentage there.

findings.title: Setting descriptions no longer match behavior
findings.description: The `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb` descriptions still call these values the maximum upload size (lines 1037-1038). After this change, images above `max_image_size_kb` are accepted and reduced, and the API URL cap is 10 MB regardless of the setting. Update the wording or the behavior.

findings.title: New resize path has no test coverage
findings.description: `spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb` covers only the small `logo.png` fixture and an oversized attachment. No test uploads an image above `max_image_size_kb` and checks the result. `spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb` has no `downsize` case, and nothing exercises the emoji job. A single test of that job would have caught the first finding.

findings.title: Other changed call sites are compatible
findings.description: I checked the other changed signatures. The removed `OptimizedImage.dimensions` helper has no remaining callers, and the `optimize` signature change is used only inside `optimized_image.rb`. The four-argument `resize` callers (`app/models/upload.rb:98`, `lib/letter_avatar.rb:48`, `lib/tasks/uploads.rake:347`) still match `resize(from, to, width, height, opts)`.
